program: BattlEye, Easy Anti-Cheat, FACEIT Anti-Cheat, Riot Vanguard
method: Structured comparison of four anti-cheats plus the Flame rootkit against seven rootkit-like metrics, using prior rootkit research, reverse-engineering write-ups and vendor documentation. No test rig. A system scoring 4 or more points is classed as rootkit-like. Table 1 sums: BattlEye 3, EAC 2, FACEIT 5, Vanguard 4, Flame 5.
conflict_reported: EAC blocks its game from starting if BattlEye's kernel driver (BEDaisy.sys) is running. FACEIT blocks execution when Hyper-V is enabled. Load timing: Vanguard and FACEIT at boot; BattlEye and EAC only when the protected game starts.
limitations: Reports no CPU, memory, FPS, boot or disk measurement. arXiv preprint. Vanguard boot behaviour predates the 2026 On-Demand option (see perf-004).
verbatim_excerpt: FACEIT Anti-Cheat and Vanguard, however, were identified as rootkit-like applications

method: PRISMA 2020 systematic literature review. 402 records identified, 88 full-text articles included, screened in Rayyan. Text says Web of Science was searched although Table 1 lists five databases.

perf_evidence.metric: Ordinal 'lack of overhead' rating, kernel-based anti-cheat driver (Lehtonen scale)

perf_evidence.condition: Review does not reconcile this with the Table 2 rating

limitations: Reports no measured FPS, CPU, memory, overhead percentage or boot figure for kernel anti-cheat. Useful as formal evidence that the literature it covers lacks such benchmarks. Its one numeric overhead (Kenali 1.5-3.5%) is a Linux kernel system that the review itself says is not an anti-cheat.
verbatim_excerpt: Detailed benchmarks are not provided, studies rely on relative scoring.

site: Microsoft 365 Message Center MC1465669 (via mc.merill.net mirror)
method: Vendor announcement. No test.
conflict_reported: From October 2026 quality updates start enabling memory integrity on more eligible devices, and on some devices VBS as well. Windows evaluates hardware capabilities, compatibility and performance considerations first. Devices where memory integrity was explicitly disabled are left alone.
limitations: Gives no performance figure. Read through a third-party mirror of the Message Center text. Analyst note: HVCI state of any test PC can change with a quality update, so it must be recorded per run.

method: Vendor support documentation. No test.

posted_date: 2015-11-24 (page date; content later updated, names UL Procyon)
method: Single test PC, OS installed and updated, Windows Update disabled during testing, Microsoft Office and Adobe Reader installed. Six automated tasks: file copying between two physical disks, archiving and unarchiving, silent application install, application launching, file download from a web server, browsing in Chrome. Each repeated at least 10 times (five with fingerprinting, five without), with a reboot after each run and an active Internet connection. File copying combines the first run on a fresh image with the mean of later runs. Times are clustered into Very Fast, Fast, Mediocre, Slow; up to 90 points, plus Procyon score, maximum 100.
limitations: Graded B as an independent lab, not an academic source. Hardware not specified on this page. The page's point labels contain an apparent typo (Fast listed at 15 and at 10). Gaming and boot are not covered.
verbatim_excerpt: For the Launching Applications test, only the scores of the subsequent runs are used to create the average.

program: Consumer security products in 19 ranks (Avast and AVG share one), including Microsoft Defender
method: Windows 11 64-bit, Intel Core i3, 8GB RAM, SSD. UL Procyon Office Productivity benchmark, with no-security-software baseline on the same machine scored at 100. Each test run multiple times, median reported.

method: Times website load, program download, standard software launch, program install, and file copy locally and over a network, each several times, against reference systems without security programs. High-end PC: Core i7-10700K, 1 TB NVMe, 16 GB RAM.

program: 23 security products plus Microsoft Security Essentials / Defender

method: Vendor security alert documentation. No test.
